```{r}

# ============================================================
# 0. LIBRARIES AND PROJECT DIRECTORY
# ============================================================

library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(sf)
library(spdep)
library(CARBayes)
library(ggplot2)
library(writexl)
library(grid)
library(stringr)
library(tibble)

if (!requireNamespace("fingertipsR", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("fingertipsR")
}

folder <- "C:/Users/ranve/Documents/Bioinformatics/Individual project"


# ============================================================
# 1. HELPER FUNCTIONS
# ============================================================

clean <- function(x) {
  stringr::str_squish(as.character(x))
}

num <- function(x) {
  suppressWarnings(as.numeric(gsub(",", "", clean(x))))
}

# Correct obsolete Barnsley and Sheffield codes if they
# occur in any of the older datasets.

correct_LAD_codes <- function(x) {
  x <- trimws(as.character(x))

  x[x == "E08000038"] <- "E08000016"
  x[x == "E08000039"] <- "E08000019"

  x
}


# ============================================================
# 2. GET SMOKING DATA
# ============================================================

smoking_data <- fingertipsR::fingertips_data(
  IndicatorID = 93085,
  AreaTypeID = 501
)

smoking_clean <- smoking_data %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    Timeperiod == "2024/25",
    AreaType == "Districts & UAs (from Apr 2023)"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    LAD24CD = correct_LAD_codes(AreaCode),
    smoking_at_delivery = num(Value)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(LAD24CD, .keep_all = TRUE)

cat("Smoking LADs:", nrow(smoking_clean), "\n")
summary(smoking_clean$smoking_at_delivery)


# ============================================================
# 3. GET MATERNAL AGE DATA
# ============================================================

age_data <- fingertipsR::fingertips_data(
  IndicatorID = 92250,
  AreaTypeID = 501
)

age_clean <- age_data %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    Timeperiod == "2024/25",
    AreaType == "Districts & UAs (from Apr 2023)"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    LAD24CD = correct_LAD_codes(AreaCode),
    maternal_age_35plus = num(Value)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(LAD24CD, .keep_all = TRUE)

cat("Maternal-age LADs:", nrow(age_clean), "\n")
summary(age_clean$maternal_age_35plus)


# ============================================================
# 4. GET OBESITY DATA
# ============================================================

# Indicator 93881 is adult obesity prevalence.
# It is not a measure of maternal obesity.

obesity_data <- tryCatch(
  fingertipsR::fingertips_data(
    IndicatorID = 93881,
    AreaTypeID = 501
  ),
  error = function(e) {
    message(
      "\nFingertips obesity API unavailable: ",
      conditionMessage(e)
    )
    NULL
  }
)

if (is.null(obesity_data)) {

  message(
    "Obesity values will be taken from the supplemental Excel file ",
    "where available. Other missing values will remain NA."
  )

  obesity_clean <- tibble::tibble(
    LAD24CD = character(),
    obesity = numeric()
  )

} else {

  obesity_clean <- obesity_data %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      Timeperiod == "2024/25",
      AreaType == "Districts & UAs (from Apr 2023)"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      LAD24CD = correct_LAD_codes(AreaCode),
      obesity = num(Value)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::distinct(LAD24CD, .keep_all = TRUE)

  cat("Obesity LADs:", nrow(obesity_clean), "\n")
  summary(obesity_clean$obesity)
}


# ============================================================
# 5. CHECK DUPLICATES IN FINGERTIPS DATA
# ============================================================

check_duplicates <- function(data, dataset_name) {

  duplicates <- data %>%
    dplyr::count(LAD24CD) %>%
    dplyr::filter(n > 1)

  if (nrow(duplicates) > 0) {

    cat("\nDuplicates in", dataset_name, ":\n")
    print(duplicates)

    stop(
      paste(
        "Duplicate LAD codes found in",
        dataset_name
      )
    )
  }
}

check_duplicates(smoking_clean, "smoking data")
check_duplicates(age_clean, "maternal age data")
check_duplicates(obesity_clean, "obesity data")


# ============================================================
# 6. COMBINE EXISTING DATA
# ============================================================

full_extension <- england_data %>%
  dplyr::select(
    LAD24CD,
    LAD24NM,
    births,
    stillbirths,
    IMD_rank,
    ethnic_minority_pct = ethnic_minority_pct.x
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    LAD24CD = correct_LAD_codes(LAD24CD)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    smoking_clean,
    by = "LAD24CD"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    age_clean,
    by = "LAD24CD"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    obesity_clean,
    by = "LAD24CD"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    stringr::str_detect(LAD24CD, "^E")
  )


# ============================================================
# 7. READ AND CORRECT THE SUPPLEMENTAL LAD DATA
# ============================================================

requested_LADs <- readxl::read_excel(
  file.path(
    folder,
    "requested_LADs_all_data.xlsx"
  )
)

# Correct the old Barnsley and Sheffield codes.

requested_LADs <- requested_LADs %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    LAD24CD = correct_LAD_codes(LAD24CD),

    LAD24NM = clean(LAD24NM)
  )

# Standardise Cornwall and Isles of Scilly.

requested_LADs <- requested_LADs %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    LAD24CD = dplyr::if_else(
      stringr::str_detect(
        LAD24CD,
        "E06000052.*E06000053|E06000053.*E06000052"
      ),
      "E06000052_E06000053",
      LAD24CD
    ),

    maternal_age_35plus = dplyr::if_else(
      live_births > 0,
      100 * maternal_age_35plus_count / live_births,
      NA_real_
    )
  )

# Check the corrected codes.

cat("\nCorrected supplemental LAD codes:\n\n")

print(
  requested_LADs %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      LAD24NM %in% c("Barnsley", "Sheffield")
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(LAD24CD, LAD24NM)
)

# Confirm the expected codes.

if (
  !all(
    c("E08000016", "E08000019") %in%
      requested_LADs$LAD24CD
  )
) {
  stop(
    "Barnsley or Sheffield is missing from the supplemental dataset."
  )
}


# ============================================================
# 8. CONVERT SUPPLEMENTAL DATA INTO MODELLING FORMAT
# ============================================================

requested_LADs_clean <- requested_LADs %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    LAD24CD,
    LAD24NM,
    births = live_births,
    stillbirths,
    IMD_rank = mean_lsoa_imd_rank,
    ethnic_minority_pct,
    smoking_at_delivery = smoking_at_delivery_value,
    maternal_age_35plus,
    obesity = obesity_value
  )


# ============================================================
# 9. CHECK SUPPLEMENTAL RECORDS FOR DUPLICATES
# ============================================================

supplement_duplicates <- requested_LADs_clean %>%
  dplyr::count(LAD24CD) %>%
  dplyr::filter(n > 1)

if (nrow(supplement_duplicates) > 0) {

  print(supplement_duplicates)

  stop(
    "Duplicate LAD codes found in the supplemental dataset."
  )
}


# ============================================================
# 10. REPLACE EXISTING VERSIONS WITH SUPPLEMENTAL RECORDS
# ============================================================

full_extension <- full_extension %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    !LAD24CD %in% requested_LADs_clean$LAD24CD
  ) %>%
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    requested_LADs_clean
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(LAD24CD)


cat("\nDATA AFTER ADDING SUPPLEMENTAL LADs\n\n")

cat(
  "Total LAD records:",
  nrow(full_extension),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Supplemental LAD records:",
  nrow(requested_LADs_clean),
  "\n"
)


# ============================================================
# 11. CHECK DUPLICATE LADs
# ============================================================

duplicate_LADs <- full_extension %>%
  dplyr::count(LAD24CD) %>%
  dplyr::filter(n > 1)

if (nrow(duplicate_LADs) > 0) {

  print(duplicate_LADs)

  stop(
    "Duplicate LAD codes found after combining datasets."
  )
}


# ============================================================
# 12. CHECK MISSING DATA
# ============================================================

cat("\nMISSING DATA CHECK\n\n")

cat("Total LADs:", nrow(full_extension), "\n")

cat(
  "Missing births:",
  sum(is.na(full_extension$births)),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Missing stillbirths:",
  sum(is.na(full_extension$stillbirths)),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Missing IMD:",
  sum(is.na(full_extension$IMD_rank)),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Missing ethnicity:",
  sum(is.na(full_extension$ethnic_minority_pct)),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Missing smoking:",
  sum(is.na(full_extension$smoking_at_delivery)),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Missing maternal age:",
  sum(is.na(full_extension$maternal_age_35plus)),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Missing obesity:",
  sum(is.na(full_extension$obesity)),
  "\n"
)


missing_full_data <- full_extension %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    is.na(births) |
      is.na(stillbirths) |
      is.na(IMD_rank) |
      is.na(ethnic_minority_pct) |
      is.na(smoking_at_delivery) |
      is.na(maternal_age_35plus) |
      is.na(obesity)
  )

cat(
  "\nLADs with missing data:",
  nrow(missing_full_data),
  "\n"
)

print(missing_full_data, n = Inf)


# ============================================================
# 13. COMPLETE CASE DATASET
# ============================================================

full_extension_complete <- full_extension %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(births),
    !is.na(stillbirths),
    !is.na(IMD_rank),
    !is.na(ethnic_minority_pct),
    !is.na(smoking_at_delivery),
    !is.na(maternal_age_35plus),
    !is.na(obesity),
    births > 0
  )

cat(
  "\nComplete LADs:",
  nrow(full_extension_complete),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Excluded LADs:",
  nrow(full_extension) -
    nrow(full_extension_complete),
  "\n"
)

# Do not fit the five-predictor model if there are insufficient
# complete observations.

if (nrow(full_extension_complete) < 2) {
  stop(
    paste(
      "Insufficient complete LAD data to fit the model.",
      "Obesity values are missing. Obtain the adult obesity",
      "indicator data from Fingertips or a downloaded CSV",
      "before proceeding."
    )
  )
}


# ============================================================
# 14. OBSERVED STILLBIRTH RATE
# ============================================================

full_extension_complete <- full_extension_complete %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    observed_rate_per_1000 =
      (stillbirths / births) * 1000
  )

summary(
  full_extension_complete$observed_rate_per_1000
)


# ============================================================
# 15. STANDARDISE COVARIATES
# ============================================================

full_extension_complete <- full_extension_complete %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    IMD_scaled =
      as.numeric(scale(IMD_rank)),

    ethnicity_scaled =
      as.numeric(scale(ethnic_minority_pct)),

    smoking_scaled =
      as.numeric(scale(smoking_at_delivery)),

    age_scaled =
      as.numeric(scale(maternal_age_35plus)),

    obesity_scaled =
      as.numeric(scale(obesity))
  )

print(
  summary(
    full_extension_complete[
      ,
      c(
        "IMD_scaled",
        "ethnicity_scaled",
        "smoking_scaled",
        "age_scaled",
        "obesity_scaled"
      )
    ]
  )
)


# ============================================================
# 16. DOWNLOAD FULL UK LAD BOUNDARIES
# ============================================================

cat("\nDownloading full UK LAD boundaries...\n")

url <- paste0(
  "https://services1.arcgis.com/ESMARspQHYMw9BZ9/arcgis/rest/services/",
  "Local_Authority_Districts_May_2024_Boundaries_UK_BGC/",
  "FeatureServer/0/query?",
  "where=1%3D1&outFields=*&f=geojson"
)

lad_uk <- sf::st_read(
  url,
  quiet = TRUE
)

# Correct the code format in the spatial data too.

lad_uk <- lad_uk %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    LAD24CD = correct_LAD_codes(LAD24CD)
  )

cat(
  "Full UK LADs downloaded:",
  nrow(lad_uk),
  "\n"
)


# ============================================================
# 17. PREPARE ENGLISH SPATIAL DATA
# ============================================================

england_sf_base <- lad_uk %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    stringr::str_detect(LAD24CD, "^E")
  ) %>%
  sf::st_make_valid()


# Check that Barnsley and Sheffield are in the boundaries.

barnsley_sheffield_check <- england_sf_base %>%
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    LAD24CD %in% c("E08000016", "E08000019")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(LAD24CD, LAD24NM)

print(barnsley_sheffield_check)

if (nrow(barnsley_sheffield_check) != 2) {
  stop(
    "Barnsley and Sheffield boundaries were not both found."
  )
}


# ============================================================
# 18. DISSOLVE CORNWALL AND ISLES OF SCILLY
# ============================================================

cornwall_scilly_sf <- england_sf_base %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    LAD24CD %in% c(
      "E06000052",
      "E06000053"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    LAD24CD = "E06000052_E06000053",
    LAD24NM = "Cornwall and Isles of Scilly",
    do_union = TRUE
  )

if (nrow(cornwall_scilly_sf) == 0) {
  stop(
    "Cornwall and Isles of Scilly polygons were not found in the boundary file."
  )
}

england_sf_model <- england_sf_base %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    !LAD24CD %in% c(
      "E06000052",
      "E06000053"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    cornwall_scilly_sf
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(LAD24CD)


# ============================================================
# 19. MATCH SPATIAL DATA TO MODELLING DATA
# ============================================================

missing_spatial_codes <- full_extension_complete %>%
  dplyr::anti_join(
    sf::st_drop_geometry(england_sf_model) %>%
      dplyr::select(LAD24CD),
    by = "LAD24CD"
  )

if (nrow(missing_spatial_codes) > 0) {

  cat("\nLADs without matching spatial boundaries:\n")

  print(
    missing_spatial_codes %>%
      dplyr::select(LAD24CD, LAD24NM)
  )

  stop(
    "Some modelled LADs do not have matching spatial boundaries."
  )
}

full_sf <- england_sf_model %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    LAD24CD %in% full_extension_complete$LAD24CD
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(
    match(
      LAD24CD,
      full_extension_complete$LAD24CD
    )
  )

cat(
  "\nSpatial LADs:",
  nrow(full_sf),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Data LADs:",
  nrow(full_extension_complete),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Order identical:",
  identical(
    full_sf$LAD24CD,
    full_extension_complete$LAD24CD
  ),
  "\n"
)

if (
  !identical(
    full_sf$LAD24CD,
    full_extension_complete$LAD24CD
  )
) {
  stop(
    "Spatial and modelling data are not in the same order."
  )
}


# ============================================================
# 20. CREATE QUEEN NEIGHBOURS AND HANDLE ISOLATED LADs
# ============================================================

# Ensure valid geometries
full_sf <- sf::st_make_valid(full_sf)

# Create Queen-contiguity neighbours
full_nb <- spdep::poly2nb(
  full_sf,
  queen = TRUE
)

# Convert Queen neighbours into an adjacency matrix
full_W <- spdep::nb2mat(
  full_nb,
  style = "B",
  zero.policy = TRUE
)

# Identify isolated LADs
zero_neighbour_idx <- which(rowSums(full_W) == 0)

cat(
  "\nLADs with zero Queen-contiguity neighbours:",
  length(zero_neighbour_idx),
  "\n"
)

if (length(zero_neighbour_idx) > 0) {

  print(
    full_sf[zero_neighbour_idx, ] %>%
      sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
      dplyr::select(LAD24CD, LAD24NM)
  )

  # Transform to British National Grid for distance calculations
  full_sf_27700 <- sf::st_transform(full_sf, 27700)

  # Use a point within each polygon to represent its location
  representative_points <- sf::st_point_on_surface(
    full_sf_27700
  )

  coordinates <- sf::st_coordinates(
    representative_points
  )

  # Calculate distances between every pair of LADs
  distance_matrix <- as.matrix(
    stats::dist(coordinates)
  )

  # Add a nearest-neighbour link for every isolated LAD
  for (i in zero_neighbour_idx) {

    # Exclude the LAD itself
    distance_matrix[i, i] <- Inf

    nearest_idx <- which.min(distance_matrix[i, ])

    # Add a symmetric connection
    full_W[i, nearest_idx] <- 1
    full_W[nearest_idx, i] <- 1

    cat(
      "Connected:",
      full_sf$LAD24NM[i],
      "<->",
      full_sf$LAD24NM[nearest_idx],
      "| Distance:",
      round(distance_matrix[i, nearest_idx]),
      "metres\n"
    )
  }
}

# Assign LAD codes to matrix rows and columns
rownames(full_W) <- full_sf$LAD24CD
colnames(full_W) <- full_sf$LAD24CD

# Final validation
cat("\nADJACENCY MATRIX VALIDATION\n")

cat("Number of LADs:", nrow(full_W), "\n")
cat("Matrix symmetric:", isSymmetric(full_W), "\n")
cat("Zero row sums:", sum(rowSums(full_W) == 0), "\n")
cat("Minimum neighbours:", min(rowSums(full_W)), "\n")
cat("Maximum neighbours:", max(rowSums(full_W)), "\n")

if (
  !isSymmetric(full_W) ||
  any(rowSums(full_W) == 0) ||
  any(diag(full_W) != 0)
) {
  stop("Adjacency matrix validation failed.")
}

# Confirm matrix order matches modelling data
if (!identical(
  rownames(full_W),
  full_extension_complete$LAD24CD
)) {
  stop("Adjacency matrix order does not match modelling data.")
}

cat("\nAdjacency matrix successfully created.\n")

# ============================================================
# 21. FINAL MODELLING DATA
# ============================================================

full_model_data <-
  as.data.frame(full_extension_complete)

model_variables <- c(
  "stillbirths",
  "births",
  "IMD_scaled",
  "ethnicity_scaled",
  "smoking_scaled",
  "age_scaled",
  "obesity_scaled"
)

print(
  colSums(
    is.na(
      full_model_data[, model_variables]
    )
  )
)

cat(
  "LADs with zero/negative births:",
  sum(full_model_data$births <= 0),
  "\n"
)

if (
  any(full_model_data$births <= 0) ||
  anyNA(full_model_data[, model_variables])
) {
  stop(
    "The modelling dataset contains missing values or invalid birth counts."
  )
}


# ============================================================
# 22. FIT FINAL FULL MODEL
# ============================================================

cat("\nFITTING FINAL FULL MODEL\n\n")

final_model <- CARBayes::S.CARleroux(
  formula =
    stillbirths ~
    IMD_scaled +
    ethnicity_scaled +
    smoking_scaled +
    age_scaled +
    obesity_scaled +
    offset(log(births)),
  family = "poisson",
  data = full_model_data,
  W = full_W,
  burnin = 10000,
  n.sample = 50000,
  thin = 1,
  n.chains = 1,
  n.cores = 1,
  verbose = TRUE
)


# ============================================================
# 23. MODEL RESULTS
# ============================================================

print(final_model)
print(final_model$summary.results)

cat(
  "\nDIC:",
  final_model$modelfit["DIC"],
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "LMPL:",
  final_model$modelfit["LMPL"],
  "\n"
)


# ============================================================
# 24. POSTERIOR COEFFICIENTS
# ============================================================

beta_samples <- final_model$samples$beta

cat(
  "Beta posterior dimensions:",
  dim(beta_samples)[1],
  "iterations x",
  dim(beta_samples)[2],
  "coefficients\n"
)

beta_names <- c(
  "Intercept",
  "IMD_scaled",
  "ethnicity_scaled",
  "smoking_scaled",
  "age_scaled",
  "obesity_scaled"
)

if (ncol(beta_samples) != length(beta_names)) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "Expected ",
      length(beta_names),
      " coefficients but found ",
      ncol(beta_samples),
      ". Check the model formula."
    )
  )
}

colnames(beta_samples) <- beta_names

beta_summary <- data.frame(
  Variable = beta_names,

  Posterior_Mean =
    apply(beta_samples, 2, mean),

  Lower_95_CrI =
    apply(
      beta_samples,
      2,
      quantile,
      probs = 0.025
    ),

  Upper_95_CrI =
    apply(
      beta_samples,
      2,
      quantile,
      probs = 0.975
    )
) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Rate_Ratio = exp(Posterior_Mean),
    RR_Lower_95_CrI = exp(Lower_95_CrI),
    RR_Upper_95_CrI = exp(Upper_95_CrI)
  )

print(beta_summary)


# ============================================================
# 25. POSTERIOR SPATIAL EFFECTS
# ============================================================

phi_samples <- final_model$samples$phi

cat(
  "\nPosterior phi dimensions:",
  dim(phi_samples)[1],
  "x",
  dim(phi_samples)[2],
  "\n"
)


# ============================================================
# 26. DESIGN MATRIX
# ============================================================

X <- stats::model.matrix(
  ~
    IMD_scaled +
    ethnicity_scaled +
    smoking_scaled +
    age_scaled +
    obesity_scaled,
  data = full_model_data
)

cat(
  "Design matrix dimensions:",
  dim(X)[1],
  "x",
  dim(X)[2],
  "\n"
)

if (ncol(X) != ncol(beta_samples)) {
  stop(
    "The design matrix and posterior coefficient dimensions do not match."
  )
}


# ============================================================
# 27. POSTERIOR LAD-SPECIFIC STILLBIRTH RATES
# ============================================================

n_post <- nrow(beta_samples)
n_lad <- nrow(full_model_data)

if (nrow(phi_samples) != n_post) {
  stop(
    "The posterior beta and phi samples have different numbers of iterations."
  )
}

if (ncol(phi_samples) != n_lad) {
  stop(
    "The number of posterior spatial effects does not match the number of LADs."
  )
}

posterior_rate <- matrix(
  NA_real_,
  nrow = n_post,
  ncol = n_lad
)

for (s in seq_len(n_post)) {

  eta <- as.numeric(
    X %*% beta_samples[s, ]
  ) + phi_samples[s, ]

  posterior_rate[s, ] <- exp(eta) * 1000
}


# ============================================================
# 28. POSTERIOR SUMMARY OF STILLBIRTH RATE
# ============================================================

posterior_mean_rate <-
  apply(posterior_rate, 2, mean)

posterior_median_rate <-
  apply(posterior_rate, 2, median)

posterior_lower_rate <-
  apply(
    posterior_rate,
    2,
    quantile,
    probs = 0.025
  )

posterior_upper_rate <-
  apply(
    posterior_rate,
    2,
    quantile,
    probs = 0.975
  )


# ============================================================
# 29. POSTERIOR HOTSPOT PROBABILITY
# ============================================================

threshold_rate <- 3.9

posterior_hotspot_probability <-
  apply(
    posterior_rate,
    2,
    function(x) mean(x > threshold_rate)
  )

cat(
  "\nPosterior probability range:",
  min(posterior_hotspot_probability),
  "to",
  max(posterior_hotspot_probability),
  "\n"
)


# ============================================================
# 30. FINAL HOTSPOT RESULTS
# ============================================================

hotspot_results <- data.frame(
  LAD24CD = full_model_data$LAD24CD,
  LAD24NM = full_model_data$LAD24NM,
  births = full_model_data$births,
  stillbirths = full_model_data$stillbirths,
  observed_rate_per_1000 = full_model_data$observed_rate_per_1000,
  posterior_mean_rate = posterior_mean_rate,
  posterior_median_rate = posterior_median_rate,
  posterior_lower_95 = posterior_lower_rate,
  posterior_upper_95 = posterior_upper_rate,
  probability_rate_above_3_9 = posterior_hotspot_probability
)


# ============================================================
# 31. HOTSPOT CLASSIFICATION
# ============================================================

hotspot_results <- hotspot_results %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    hotspot_probability_category =
      dplyr::case_when(
        probability_rate_above_3_9 >= 0.95 ~
          "Very high probability",
        probability_rate_above_3_9 >= 0.80 ~
          "High probability",
        probability_rate_above_3_9 >= 0.50 ~
          "Moderate probability",
        probability_rate_above_3_9 >= 0.20 ~
          "Low probability",
        TRUE ~
          "Very low probability"
      ),

    hotspot_95 =
      probability_rate_above_3_9 >= 0.95
  )


# ============================================================
# 32. TOP HOTSPOTS
# ============================================================

top_hotspots <- hotspot_results %>%
  dplyr::arrange(
    dplyr::desc(probability_rate_above_3_9)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    LAD24CD,
    LAD24NM,
    observed_rate_per_1000,
    posterior_mean_rate,
    posterior_lower_95,
    posterior_upper_95,
    probability_rate_above_3_9
  )

print(utils::head(top_hotspots, 20))

# 33. HIGH-PROBABILITY HOTSPOTS
# ============================================================

cat("\nHOTSPOT RESULTS\n\n")

cat(

)

cat("Number of LADs:", n_lad, "\n")

high_probability_hotspots <- hotspot_results %>%
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# 32. LEAVE-ONE-OUT CROSS-VALIDATION (LOOCV)
# ============================================================

library(CARBayes)
library(spdep)
library(sf)
library(writexl)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. CHECK DATA AND SPATIAL ORDER
# ------------------------------------------------------------

n <- nrow(full_model_data)

stopifnot(
  nrow(full_sf) == n,
  identical(
    full_sf$LAD24CD,
    full_model_data$LAD24CD
  )
)

observed <- full_model_data$stillbirths

predicted <- numeric(n)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. CREATE THE FULL SPATIAL WEIGHTS MATRIX
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Use Queen contiguity, matching the final model.

nb_full_loocv <- spdep::poly2nb(
  full_sf,
  queen = TRUE
)

W_full_loocv <- spdep::nb2mat(
  nb_full_loocv,
  style = "B",
  zero.policy = TRUE
)


# Add nearest-neighbour links for originally isolated LADs.

zero_idx <- which(
  rowSums(W_full_loocv) == 0
)

if(length(zero_idx) > 0){

  full_points <- sf::st_point_on_surface(
    sf::st_transform(full_sf, 27700)
  )

  distance_matrix <- as.matrix(
    stats::dist(
      sf::st_coordinates(full_points)
    )
  )

  for(j in zero_idx){

    distance_matrix[j, j] <- Inf

    nearest <- which.min(
      distance_matrix[j, ]
    )

    W_full_loocv[j, nearest] <- 1
    W_full_loocv[nearest, j] <- 1

  }

}


# Ensure symmetric binary weights.

W_full_loocv <- ifelse(
  (W_full_loocv + t(W_full_loocv)) > 0,
  1,
  0
)

diag(W_full_loocv) <- 0

stopifnot(
  isSymmetric(W_full_loocv),
  all(rowSums(W_full_loocv) > 0)
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. SET UP CROSS-VALIDATION
# ------------------------------------------------------------

set.seed(123)

for(i in 1:n){

  message(
    "Running LAD ",
    i,
    " of ",
    n
  )


  # Remove the held-out LAD.

  train_data <- full_model_data[-i, ]

  train_sf <- full_sf[-i, ]


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 4. STANDARDISE USING TRAINING DATA ONLY
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  predictors <- c(
    "IMD_rank",
    "ethnic_minority_pct",
    "smoking_at_delivery",
    "maternal_age_35plus",
    "obesity"
  )

  scaled_names <- c(
    "IMD_scaled",
    "ethnicity_scaled",
    "smoking_scaled",
    "age_scaled",
    "obesity_scaled"
  )


  test_data <- full_model_data[i, ]


  for(j in seq_along(predictors)){

    variable <- predictors[j]
    scaled_variable <- scaled_names[j]

    training_mean <- mean(
      train_data[[variable]]
    )

    training_sd <- sd(
      train_data[[variable]]
    )

    if(
      !is.finite(training_sd) ||
      training_sd == 0
    ){
      stop(
        paste(
          "Invalid standard deviation for",
          variable,
          "in fold",
          i
        )
      )
    }

    train_data[[scaled_variable]] <-
      (
        train_data[[variable]] -
          training_mean
      ) / training_sd

    test_data[[scaled_variable]] <-
      (
        test_data[[variable]] -
          training_mean
      ) / training_sd

  }


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 5. CREATE TRAINING SPATIAL WEIGHTS
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  W_train <- W_full_loocv[
    -i,
    -i,
    drop = FALSE
  ]


  # Removing a LAD can leave some training LADs isolated.
  # Add nearest-neighbour links where necessary.

  zero_train_idx <- which(
    rowSums(W_train) == 0
  )

  if(length(zero_train_idx) > 0){

    train_points <- sf::st_point_on_surface(
      sf::st_transform(train_sf, 27700)
    )

    train_distances <- as.matrix(
      stats::dist(
        sf::st_coordinates(train_points)
      )
    )

    for(j in zero_train_idx){

      train_distances[j, j] <- Inf

      nearest <- which.min(
        train_distances[j, ]
      )

      W_train[j, nearest] <- 1
      W_train[nearest, j] <- 1

    }

  }


  W_train <- ifelse(
    (W_train + t(W_train)) > 0,
    1,
    0
  )

  diag(W_train) <- 0

  stopifnot(
    isSymmetric(W_train),
    all(rowSums(W_train) > 0),
    nrow(W_train) == nrow(train_data)
  )


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 6. FIT THE FIVE-PREDICTOR CAR LEROUX MODEL
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  model <- CARBayes::S.CARleroux(

    formula =
      stillbirths ~
      IMD_scaled +
      ethnicity_scaled +
      smoking_scaled +
      age_scaled +
      obesity_scaled +
      offset(log(births)),

    family = "poisson",

    data = train_data,

    W = W_train,

    burnin = 10000,

    n.sample = 50000,

    thin = 1,

    n.chains = 1,

    n.cores = 1,

    verbose = FALSE

  )


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 7. EXTRACT POSTERIOR SAMPLES
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  beta_draws <- model$samples$beta
  phi_draws <- model$samples$phi
  rho_draws <- as.numeric(model$samples$rho)
  tau2_draws <- as.numeric(model$samples$tau2)


  if(
    ncol(beta_draws) != 6 ||
    ncol(phi_draws) != nrow(train_data) ||
    nrow(beta_draws) != nrow(phi_draws) ||
    length(rho_draws) != nrow(beta_draws) ||
    length(tau2_draws) != nrow(beta_draws)
  ){

    stop(
      paste(
        "Posterior sample dimensions do not match in fold",
        i
      )
    )

  }


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 8. FIXED-EFFECT PREDICTION FOR HELD-OUT LAD
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  x_test <- c(
    1,
    test_data$IMD_scaled,
    test_data$ethnicity_scaled,
    test_data$smoking_scaled,
    test_data$age_scaled,
    test_data$obesity_scaled
  )

  eta_fixed <- as.numeric(
    beta_draws %*% x_test
  ) + log(test_data$births)


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 9. PREDICT THE HELD-OUT SPATIAL EFFECT
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  # Obtain the held-out LAD's connections to the training LADs.

  w_heldout <- W_full_loocv[
    i,
    -i
  ]

  # If it has no remaining training neighbours,
  # connect it to its nearest training LAD.

  if(sum(w_heldout) == 0){

    full_points <- sf::st_point_on_surface(
      sf::st_transform(full_sf, 27700)
    )

    heldout_coordinates <- sf::st_coordinates(
      full_points[i, ]
    )

    training_coordinates <- sf::st_coordinates(
      full_points[-i, ]
    )

    distances <- sqrt(
      rowSums(
        (
          training_coordinates -
            matrix(
              heldout_coordinates,
              nrow = nrow(training_coordinates),
              ncol = 2,
              byrow = TRUE
            )
        )^2
      )
    )

    nearest <- which.min(distances)

    w_heldout[nearest] <- 1

  }


  # Conditional CAR Leroux spatial-effect prediction:
  #
  # E(phi_i | phi_-i) =
  # rho * sum(w_ij * phi_j) /
  # (1 - rho + rho * sum(w_ij))
  #
  # Conditional variance =
  # tau2 / (1 - rho + rho * sum(w_ij))

  heldout_degree <- sum(w_heldout)

  spatial_mean <- numeric(nrow(phi_draws))
  spatial_variance <- numeric(nrow(phi_draws))

  for(s in 1:nrow(phi_draws)){

    denominator <-
      1 - rho_draws[s] +
      rho_draws[s] * heldout_degree

    spatial_mean[s] <-
      rho_draws[s] *
      sum(
        w_heldout * phi_draws[s, ]
      ) / denominator

    spatial_variance[s] <-
      tau2_draws[s] / denominator

  }


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 10. PREDICT EXPECTED STILLBIRTH COUNT
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  # Integrate over the conditional distribution of the
  # held-out spatial effect using the log-normal expectation.

  predicted_draws <- exp(
    eta_fixed +
      spatial_mean +
      0.5 * spatial_variance
  )

  predicted[i] <- mean(predicted_draws)


}


# ============================================================
# 11. CROSS-VALIDATION PERFORMANCE
# ============================================================

rmse <- sqrt(
  mean(
    (observed - predicted)^2
  )
)

mae <- mean(
  abs(
    observed - predicted
  )
)

bias <- mean(
  predicted - observed
)


# ============================================================
# 12. RESULTS
# ============================================================

results <- data.frame(

  LAD = full_model_data$LAD24CD,

  LAD_name = full_model_data$LAD24NM,

  observed = observed,

  predicted = predicted,

  error = predicted - observed

)


print(rmse)
print(mae)
print(bias)


# ============================================================
# 13. EXPORT RESULTS
# ============================================================

write_xlsx(

  list(

    predictions = results,

    validation = data.frame(
      RMSE = rmse,
      MAE = mae,
      Bias = bias
    )

  ),

  file.path(
    folder,
    "LOOCV_full_model.xlsx"
  )

)
```
